_what: The computer entry's own settings, read once by src/native_entry/computer.rs: the size limits of its config, key and receipt files, the receipt file each account folder holds, the app key-value file name (relative to the account folder, the name the engine's own tests use), the one origin scheme a computer accepts, the stop poll and the stop grace, and the forwarder session timings (connect and read limits, and the wait before a computer opens its next session to the forwarder, and the point in a session's life where the next one opens). How many accounts the computer holds is not here: it is the `accounts` limit (src/account/computers/settings.json `limits`), the shipped row (old trillion's `accounts_max`, 256) raised by the computer config's `access` rows. The account rows store values are not here: they are the computer config's `sign_in` (src/account/rows.rs `ComputerSignIn`), and an account's starting rows are its `new_accounts`; sign-in itself is the Better Auth Workshop tool (src/account/signed_in.rs). The computer config's fields are named in computer.rs. Adding a computer (computer/join.rs): `lock_file` is the account folder's startup lock, which stays at its computer and never goes in a taken copy; `copy_manifest` is the manifest a taken copy describes itself in (written last, at most `copy_manifest_max_bytes`, format `copy_version`); `joining_marker` is the file a joined account folder holds until its copies have caught up once (until then the computer neither claims the writer row nor votes for a takeover). A computer named in an account's row starts holding it by itself (computer/join_itself.rs): its `Message::Holding` answer (the receipt, object index, key row and computers row) travels in parts when it is longer than one message between computers (`message_body_bytes`), up to `carried_bytes` (src/account/computers/settings.json); the account stores come through the writer's feed as records (src/account/computers/account_stores.rs); and the computer that made an account tells each other computer of its row at once, every `tell_copy_keepers_wait_ms`, at most `tell_copy_keepers_tries` times, until each holds it. The command line changes an account's rows directly and tells the process that serves the folder with SIGUSR1 only when that process holds the folder's `lock_file` and is named in `outside_changes_marker` (its pid), so the change travels as an acknowledged change (`Copies::copy_outside_changes`); a computer that has not caught up its other computers tries again every `tell_copy_keepers_wait_ms`, at most `tell_copy_keepers_tries` times. A computer the row lets answer that joined an account and has no copy of its tools takes the live copy of another computer of the account that may answer (`Message::Tools`, src/tool_runs/tools/install.rs `take_copy`), at most `tools_page_bytes` of file bytes per page (each page in parts when longer than one message), checked against that computer's manifest and receipt. A computer that already serves an account the row lets it answer and starts with no copy of its tools (lost or removed) asks the same way first, every `tools_from_computer_wait_ms` while its sessions open, at most `tools_from_computer_tries` times, then installs from the network as at a first start. Taking an account the hosting app holds (computer/hosted.rs) uses `lock_file` and `receipt_file`. Nothing here names a machine kind or a vendor. `tell_origins_tries`: on each new forwarder session the computer hands every account's origins row in again (src/native_entry/computer/installations.rs; the forwarder keeps them in memory only), one try every `renew_every_ms` of the computers settings, at most this many times, until each is taken.
